description: Section 7 exact checkout calculator (convenience fee + GST-on-fee) in integer INR paise with the mandatory 121481-paise fixture, plus the immutable quote snapshot contract (cart revision, expiry, snapshot hash, policy version). This is the single highest-risk gap: no convenience/GST calculator exists today and the checkout handler charges the bare Wix supply total. Pure arithmetic + data, no AWS. INDEPENDENT of all other features except that FEAT-004 wires it in.
steps: Create amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/checkout_pricing.py implementing the exact formula from section 7 using Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP and integer paise, reusing money.py Money/positive_paise: convenienceFeePaise = round_half_up(collectionBeforeConveniencePaise * 250 / 10000); convenienceGstPaise = round_half_up(convenienceFeePaise * 1800 / 10000); totalPayablePaise = collection + fee + gst. collectionBeforeConveniencePaise is the authoritative approved collection total AFTER supply GST/discounts/delivery and EXCLUDES the convenience fee and its GST. Reject negative/overflow/fractional-paise/non-INR; define zero-total behavior that never pretends an uncharged order is a captured payment.

Store rounded components (collection, fee, gst, total) and a calculation policy version string. Reconcile CGST/SGST vs IGST splits to the exact total. Keep seller GSTIN 19AAFFW7196L1Z8 distinct from any buyer GSTIN; do not double-add GST where catalog pricing is inclusive and surface a concrete conflict rather than silently adding.

Create an immutable quote snapshot dataclass/builder (e.g. in checkout_pricing.py or a new quote.py) carrying cart revision, expiry timestamp, snapshot hash (stable hash over frozen customer/site/cart/item/address/delivery/component data), and policy version. A cart edit yields a NEW quote; never mutate an existing paid or unresolved snapshot.

Add tests/test_checkout_pricing.py: MUST include the exact fixture for a tax-exclusive 1000 INR supply -> supply GST 180, collection 1180 (118000 paise), fee 29.50 (2950 paise), GST on fee 5.31 (531 paise), payable 1214.81 == 121481 paise. Also cover: fractional-paise rejection, negative/overflow rejection, non-INR rejection, zero-total behavior, rounding boundaries (round-half-up ties), CGST/SGST reconciles to total, quote snapshot hash stability and expiry, and that editing the cart produces a different quote hash.
acceptance_criteria: A new pytest asserts the 121481-paise fixture exactly and passes under .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_checkout_pricing.py
The calculator rejects floats, fractional paise, negative, overflow and non-INR inputs with a raised error (not silent rounding)
The full suite .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q stays green (>= 5607 passed plus the new tests, 0 failed)
The quote snapshot exposes cart revision, expiry, snapshot hash and policy version and is immutable
findings: Implemented in commit 99eed122 on branch stack. New files: amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/checkout_pricing.py and tests/test_checkout_pricing.py (762 insertions). round_half_up uses Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP over integer basis points (250/10000 fee, 1800/10000 GST) with a 10000 denominator; no floats on any money path. compute_quote reuses money.Money and the money.py ceiling (9007199254740991) for bounds; rejects float, bool, fractional-Decimal, negative, overflow (checked on both input and total) and non-INR. collectionBeforeConveniencePaise is treated strictly as an input (supply GST/discount/delivery already applied) so inclusive catalog pricing is never double-taxed. CheckoutQuote is a frozen dataclass storing rounded collection/fee/gst/total + CALCULATION_POLICY_VERSION='checkout-pricing-2026-10-01', seller GSTIN 19AAFFW7196L1Z8 (constant, distinct from buyer which is an arg and rejected if equal/malformed), and a TaxSplit that reconciles CGST+SGST (odd paise to CGST) or IGST exactly to the GST. Zero collection yields a valid quote with is_payable/requires_payment False and as_payable_money() raising, so an uncharged order is never treated as a capture. QuoteSnapshot is a frozen dataclass built by build_snapshot(): sha256 over a canonicalised payload (customer/site/cart id+revision/items/address/delivery/components/policyVersion) gives a stable 64-char hash; a cart edit (revision/items/address/amount) changes the hash and the original object is untouched; is_expired(now) uses an absolute created_at+ttl expiry. VERIFICATION: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_checkout_pricing.py -q => 35 passed; full suite .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q => 5643 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (baseline was 5607 passed/1 skipped; +35 new tests, one additional count is parametrized expansion). The 121481-paise fixture (118000 + 2950 + 531) asserts exactly. NOTE for FEAT-004: wire the checkout handler to compute payable via compute_quote(...).as_payable_money() instead of the raw Wix total, gating on is_payable; the module is pure arithmetic/data with no AWS. Did not push or open a PR per instructions. Untracked .agents/ task-state dir was left unstaged (not part of the repo).
